completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented the full 5-phase plan for task 350: a books-domain record pinning the approvals-stage absent-or-stale detection signature and rulings, a read-only recognizer script (books-approvals-signal.sh) emitting a user_decision offering enter-review-now/defer/decline with blocking:false and recommended=defer, a 76-case forgery-probed fixture suite, and the cross-cutting detection rule wired into both books implementation agents. Demonstrated end to end that the recognizer's emitted object reaches verdict=ask_user verbatim through orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, with the honest-red half (status unchanged, nothing written) confirmed via a --dry-run scratch run. Two deviations recorded: the books extension is not loaded in this repository so the literal deploy-to-.claude/ demonstration could not be observed here (deploy-headless.sh's own internal full gate still passed 36/0), and the final phase's full gate set was discharged against the dispatch file's Batch Gate Deferral directive (scoped narrowing invocations) rather than independently re-run.

memory_candidates.content: When an agent-system source-store doc (agents/*.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, commands/*.md, README.md, EXTENSION.md) must bare-name a script owned by an external/consumer repository (never shipped from this repo, e.g. a consuming component's own approve.sh), declare it in that extension's manifest.json top-level external_scripts array rather than provides.scripts. check-extension-docs.sh Rule E (check_referenced_scripts_declared) hard-fails on an undeclared bare *.sh/*.sql token in those five doc locations; external_scripts is the sanctioned escape hatch for a name that will never resolve to any provides.scripts entry anywhere in this repo.

To prove a user_decision-producing mechanism reaches orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's verdict=ask_user relay end to end without touching the real repository, build an isolated scratch fixture: a scratch task directory with its own .return-meta.json carrying the user_decision object, a scratch state.json (minimal active_projects entry), and a pre-created {dirname(state_file)}/.orchestration/.orchestrator-multi-state-{session_id}.json (the script hard-requires this file to already exist -- it errors with 'resolved defect store not found' otherwise). Call the script with --handoff-expected false and --dry-run, then diff the emitted object's user_decision field (jq -c) against the producer's own output for a byte-for-byte verbatim check, and confirm git status --porcelain on the real repo is unchanged before/after.

A shell self-check that greps a script's source for 'forbidden' command names (to assert it never invokes them) produces false positives when the script legitimately builds user-facing text naming those same commands (e.g. relaying '/approve' or 'approve.sh' as a string for a human to type). Fix: strip single- and double-quoted string CONTENTS first (sed -E 's/"[^"]*"//g; s/'"'"'[^'"'"']*'"'"'//g'), then search the remainder -- this isolates genuine invocation syntax from mere mention, since legitimate text in a well-written script lives inside quotes.
